channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave Woes Risk Shutting Down AI Junk Market: Credit Weekly
item.description: Junk bond buyers are increasingly freezing out tech startups looking for financing, as CoreWeave Inc.’s pain raises bigger questions about how artificial intelligence companies will fund themselves.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Schwartz and Josie Reich

item.title: Northwell CEO Says Health Care Model Must Change
item.description: Northwell Health President and CEO Dr. John D’Angelo tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the traditional US health care model is unsustainable and that improving affordability will require a greater focus on wellness, prevention and chronic disease. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, D’Angelo discusses workforce shortages, the financial pressures facing nonprofit hospitals and how AI could reduce administrative burdens while preserving the human role in consequential medical decisions. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Can the Fed Fight Inflation Without Hurting Farmers?
item.description: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee traveled to rural Illinois to hear directly from farmers facing lower crop prices and rising costs for fuel, fertilizer and other inputs. Those conversations offer the Fed a ground-level view of inflation pressures that may emerge before they are fully reflected in national data. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Freeland Warns US Alliances Are Fraying
item.description: Former Canadian Deputy Prime Minister Chrystia Freeland tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Canada and other democracies must become less reliant on the US while remaining open to rebuilding the Western alliance. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Freeland discusses Alberta’s separatist movement, President Donald Trump’s approach to Russia and Ukraine, and lessons from her negotiations with the US that inform her new book, Unreliable Boyfriend. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sports Fashion Finds a Growing Female Audience
item.description: Terez founder and CEO Zara Terez Tisch tells Bloomberg This Weekend how the growing number of women sports fans is creating new demand for fashionable team apparel and expanding opportunities for her company across professional sports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: Tesla's Roadster, Zuckerberg vs pint of Guinness, retirees not spending for pleasure, and AI born false memories: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Global Aid Cuts Deepen Humanitarian Strain
item.description: International Rescue Committee President and CEO David Miliband tells Bloomberg This Weekend that cuts in US and European aid are weakening the humanitarian response as conflicts and other crises intensify around the world. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Miliband discusses conditions in Ukraine, Yemen and Sudan, the challenge of containing disease outbreaks and the potential benefits and risks of AI in humanitarian work. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rockstar Rebuilt Itself to Make GTA VI
item.description: Bloomberg News video game reporter Jason Schreier tells Bloomberg This Weekend how Rockstar Games nearly doubled its workforce and overhauled its production culture while building the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI. Speaking with hosts Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo, Schreier explains Rockstar’s efforts to curb excessive overtime, the extraordinary commercial expectations for the game and why the company believes its next major release could take less time to develop. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Puts New Russia Sanctions on Hold
item.description: Bloomberg News Russia economy and government editor Anthony Halpin and White House correspondent Jeff Mason tell Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s waiver of new Russia sanctions could offer Moscow economic and diplomatic opportunities while adding pressure on Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stellantis Plans to Hire Hundreds More Engineers in Europe, US
item.description: Stellantis NV Chief Engineering and Technology Officer Ned Curic plans to continue hiring more engineers as the automaker rolls out dozens of new models as part of its turnaround plan.
item.dc:creator: Albertina Torsoli

item.title: Oil Trader Yaoyao Liu Who Made Billions for Vitol Is Leaving
item.description: Yaoyao Liu, whose trading in oil derivatives made billions of dollars for Vitol Group over a career marked by dramatic highs and lows, is leaving the commodities trading giant.
item.dc:creator: Alfred Cang, Archie Hunter, Lucia Kassai and Jack Farchy

item.title: David Byrne Explains How Forgotten Ideas Come Back to Life
item.description: History is littered with ideas that have been tossed aside, only for them to gain relevance at some later date. Think of Moby-Dick: forgotten in Melville’s time, but now regarded as the great American novel. Or the work of economist Hyman Minsky, which became influential a decade after his death, when the 2008 financial crisis made “the Minsky Moment”a mainstream term. These are just a couple of the things we talk about with the legendary musician David Byrne on today’s podcast. Byrne’s new book
item.dc:creator: Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway

item.title: China Warns Corrupt Officials Can’t Expect a Safe Landing
item.description: China’s top anti-graft authorities warned that officials who engage in corruption cannot expect a “safe landing,” regardless of their rank, past contributions or whether they’ve retired, according to a commentary from the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and National Commission of Supervision.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Japan’s Takaichi to Attend APEC in China if Parliament Allows
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said she plans to attend the APEC leaders summit hosted by China if parliament permits, confirming her willingness to visit amid a deep freeze of ties between the two Asian economies.
item.dc:creator: Sakura Murakami

item.title: Fairfax’s Watsa Bets On IDBI Payoff As India Booms, Report Says
item.description: Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa is betting that his Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd.’s acquisition of IDBI Bank Ltd. will pay off given India’s growth prospects, the Economic Times reported.
item.dc:creator: Siddhi Nayak

item.title: India Halts Sugar Diversion to Ethanol After El Nino Hurts Crops
item.description: India has ordered state-owned fuel retailers to stop procuring ethanol made from sugar and key sugarcane-based feedstocks in move that may help keep a lid on prices of the sweetener.
item.dc:creator: Rakesh Sharma and Pratik Parija

item.title: China Encourages Cinemas to Add Sports Events and Lottery Sales
item.description: China is encouraging cinemas to screen major sporting events, host sports activities and sell sports lottery tickets as part of a drive to link moviegoing with sports consumption, according to a notice from the National Film Administration and General Administration of Sport.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: India Frees ‘Cockroach’ Leader As Voter-List Row Simmers
item.description: The founder of India’s “Cockroach” protest movement was released on Saturday after being taken into police custody, according to its legal affairs head, as a widening fight over the country’s voter rolls keeps New Delhi on edge.
item.dc:creator: Asmi Bhatia and Akriti Sharma

item.title: Indonesia Unveils $117 Million in Fines After MSCI Warning
item.description: Indonesia announced about $117 million in fines tied to manipulative market practices involving three companies, hours after global index provider MSCI Inc. said it was weighing a downgrade of the country’s stock market over investability concerns.
item.dc:creator: Prima Wirayani and Norman Harsono
